title: The Inult's Ordeal
text: So, the next act was about to begin. Such was the scene backstage, I say.
“What is this act!? Don’t screw around!”
Ren drew his sword, huffing and puffing with rage.
“I agree with you there, bro! I know you said you’d let us perform, but this is too much! What even is this!”

“That’s why I checked with you so many times about whether we should really do this… I won’t deny it’s awful. But well, Melromarc… has such strong prejudice against demi-humans and beastmen that this kind of act goes over way too well. You heard the cheers just now, right?”
“This country is trash! Die, humans!”
“Ren… the inult persona has really soaked into you…”
Father muttered, looking at him with pitying eyes.
“Luna gently caught Keel-kun and Ama as they fell~ It was so cute~”
Luna wore an extremely radiant, blissful expression, clearly thoroughly satisfied with the performance.
“But throwing things at Keel-kun and Ama was awful~ Should Luna use magic on those people on the way home?”
“I’d really rather you didn’t.”
“Naofumi, you… you knew and still made us do this act!?”
What was this now? What was there to complain about? After all the trouble I’d gone to setting things up for them, this attitude was hardly commendable, I say.
“I knew it was awful, that’s exactly why I checked with you so many times.”
“Keel!”
“I didn’t even know it’d be like this!”
“But Keel-kun, you saw the act I was doing with Theo and Shion backstage, didn’t you? You should have known.”
“Ugh… I knew, but… I thought you’d give me and Sword Bro a cooler act than this!”
“That kind of thing is more Zeltoble’s specialty… Though for you two, it’d probably end up being a petting corner rather than an act, or maybe jumping through a ring of fire.”
No matter how hard they tried, Keel and Ren simply couldn’t take part in a flashy act in their current forms. At best, they were suited for pitiful victim roles like the one tonight.
“Aww… isn’t there anything else?”
“If there is one, it’s being tied to a roulette wheel for Lars-chan’s knife-throwing act. Want to try it?”
“Ugh… that’s genuinely terrifying, so even if I don’t get hit, I still don’t want it.”
“No, actually a few knives are meant to hit you in that act. It’s rigged so the human side never fails.”

The beastmen were made to play the roles that got hurt or failed, I say. There was, to some degree, a wholesome flow to how things were run, but even within Melromarc, only a small fraction of acts managed to avoid any discrimination creeping in. Well, in Panda’s case, her skill was good enough that her act had become pretty normal and actually earned applause. Having a talent really does save you.
“Lars-neechan and the others have it good…”
“I guess skill really matters, huh.”
“If you like, why not just cast an illusion on them? The audience would be deluded into thinking they enjoyed whatever act they wanted to see.”
Rafumi, who had been silently watching until now, offered this proposal.

“That sounds like it’d end with every audience member wearing some blissed-out grin, all seeing something different, and us basically running a shop selling sketchy drugs or hallucinations. We’d get shut down.”
Typical Rafumi. Her proposed idea got shot down immediately.
“Hmm… well, fine. It’ll make for a good memory for Azott too.”
“It is not fine! There’s no way being humiliated like this counts as good!”
“Being laughed at now and then is just part of life, Azott. Nothing is more pathetic and mockable than your lonely Christmas.”
“What is with that phrase!? Stop treating me like some loner!”
Since it was Rafumi’s own reasoning for having made him, I had no complaints about it. Though honestly, I had no idea what this “lonely Christmas” business was even about.
“Naofumi, is this really okay for your circus?”
Ren started nitpicking the act again.

“I understand how you feel. But without acts like this… Melromarc just won’t let us get away with it, otherwise… I’ll be honest with you, Ren, selling the raiders who come attack us as slaves to Siltvelt would actually be more profitable.”
“…That’s genuinely awful. Whoever enjoys this kind of thing is the real villain! They should be enslaved themselves!”
Ren was trembling with anger over something.
“Anyway, you really saved us. I’ll make you something special for dinner later as thanks, so cheer up.”
“Seriously!? Nice one, Sword Bro! He’s gonna make us something special!”
“Hey. What are you getting won over for?”
“But it’s no use, right? Complaining doesn’t seem to help anyway.”
“Ngh…”

If he hated it that much, I figured he could just leave, but for some reason Ren wasn’t straying far from the circus anymore. By my analysis, Rafumi had stolen his rightful place, and yet in his inult form there wasn’t really anywhere else for him to go, plus Luna would chase him wherever he went, so he’d more or less given up, I’d say. There was probably also the fact that, quietly, the place was actually comfortable for him. After all, back in the first world too, Ren apparently found it comfortable once he settled into Father’s village.
“Sword Bro, sure it was awful, but if the money we earn from this lets us buy back everyone from the village, and helps kids who are going through similarly awful stuff, maybe it’s not so bad.”
“Hmph! Use the money from selling off the trash instead. That’d work just as well, wouldn’t it, Naofumi? A fine slave trader you are.”
“Ren’s getting corrupted in a bad direction…”
And so, tonight’s circus was, in its own way, a great success. Things were finally getting on track, I say.
And so, after the performance ended, it was time for the after-party.
“Wolf~ Keel-kun~ Ren~ Dinner’s ready~”
“Woof!”
“Oh! Bro, is dinner done?”
“I sense malice in that calling order!!!”

Ren shouted this out especially loudly when Father called everyone in for the celebratory thank-you meal he’d made. Whatever was wrong with him now? After Father had gone to the trouble of making something special, raising a protest like this was awfully selfish of Ren, I say.
“What’s wrong, Ren?”
“Don’t ‘what’s wrong’ me! And you, Wolf, was it? What’s with that ‘Woof!’ Answer properly!”
“Well, I was just acting up until a moment ago, and this is how I’ve always gotten fed before too… What exactly is the problem?”
“Yeah, Sword Bro. What exactly’s your problem?”
Indeed. I too had no idea whatsoever what Ren was protesting about.
“Um… oh! Ren, Keel-kun, Wolf?”
“Woof!?”
This time it was Wolf who looked dissatisfied. Apparently he cared about the pecking order.
“That’s not it! It’s not about the order! It’s not like I’m complaining because I wasn’t called first!”
Ren remained dissatisfied.
“Stop lumping me into that category in the first place!”
“Huh?”
“Well… I can’t say I don’t understand what he’s getting at…”
Éclair, who had taken part today in the circus on the human side, showed some understanding of Ren’s grievance.
“But, Amaki-dono, that in itself would… well, count as discrimination, wouldn’t it.”
“I may have ended up like this, but I’m still human!”
“Could it be you didn’t like being called in the same group as Wolf and Keel-kun?”

Ren crossed his arms, clearly unhappy. Naturally, Luna was gazing at him with utter delight. Well, the three of them were, quite literally, a pack of dogs. Wolf was a fine specimen of a wolfman, while Keel and Ren were both stuck in dog form.
“I understand Iwatani-dono’s feelings. When the three of them are together, they do look quite friendly. Doesn’t that seem like it could make for an act?”
“True, I’ve been thinking something with Wolf, Keel-kun, and Ren together might work well.”
“Indeed.”
“Don’t ‘indeed’ me!”
“For a safe act, maybe something like… showing off their sense of smell? It could be fun to have the three of them compete over who’s the best at it.”
“That might work. Blindfold them and see which one gets it right.”
